Airway placement was confirmed bronchoscopically, and airflow through gastric channels and oropharyngeal leak pathways was assessed. Results: As inspiratory pressure increased, esophageal pressure rose across all devices. Dual-channel second-generation SGAs transmitted lower esophageal pressures than single-channel and first-generation devices, indicating reduced gastric insufflation and distention under high-pressure ventilation. Conclusion: SGA design significantly influences esophageal pressure transmission during cardiac arrest ventilation. Dual-channel second-generation SGAs reduce esophageal pressurization, suggesting a mechanism to mitigate gastric distention during CPR. These findings have direct implications for OHCA airway strategy, supporting device selection and ventilation approaches that minimize hyperventilation and its downstream hemodynamic consequences during resuscitation.
nc5bcbaf4c74d: Introduction: During CPR, chest compressions induce oscillations in the capnogram that can be quantified as the Capnogram Oscillation Magnitude (COM) and the Airway Opening Index (AOI). These metrics are hypothesized to reflect airway patency and effective ventilation. Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) may modulate capnographic waveform morphology during CPR, though the relationship between PEEP, COM, AOI, and hemodynamics remains poorly understood. Aim: We examined the effect of titrated PEEP on capnographic waveform morphology, including COM, AOI, and peak end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2) during mechanical CPR in a pilot study using a swine model of ventricular fibrillation (VF) cardiac arrest. Methods: Four swine underwent 8 minutes of untreated VF followed by 60 minutes of mechanical CPR. Animals were intubated and ventilated at 10 breaths/min with fraction of inspired oxygen of 1.0. PEEP was sequentially titrated across 6-minute epochs of 0, 5, and 10 cmH 2 O in repeated cycles during CPR. 6 doses of epinephrine (0.02 mg/kg) were administered beginning at minute 14 and repeated every 4 minutes. Continuous capnography and aortic blood pressure were recorded throughout. A custom MATLAB algorithm was used to calculate COM and AOI. Results: Across 4 animals, we observed that stepwise increases in PEEP from 0 to 5 to 10 cmH2O were associated with longer time to peak ETCO2 within ventilation cycles (Figure 1). We observed no overall changes in aortic pressure or ETCO2 with PEEP titrations, but these did gradually decrease over the course of resuscitation (Figure 2). Conclusion: In this preliminary swine model of cardiac arrest, increasing PEEP appeared to influence capnographic waveform morphology during mechanical CPR, particularly the time to peak ETCO2 after a ventilation. Aortic blood pressure and overall ETCO2 remained largely stable during stepwise PEEP titration, but decreased over the course of resuscitation. This association may indicate that at higher PEEP levels cardiac output exceeds ventilation, resulting in the prolonged time to peak ETCO2. Ongoing analysis will quantify the dose-dependent effects of PEEP on ventilation metrics (AOI, COM, and peak ETCO2), along with indicators of cardiac output (aortic blood pressure and the area under the capnography waveform curve). These findings may inform PEEP as a modifiable ventilation parameter during CPR to optimize airway management and resuscitation outcomes.
nf9222264f10d: Background: Psychiatric morbidity is common after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet whether survivors carry excess risk relative to other critically ill patients or instead share post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) mechanisms remains unclear. Hypothesis: OHCA survivors experience excess new-onset mental health and addictions (MHA) risk compared with matched critical illness survivors, beyond what is explained by pre-existing psychiatric history and sociodemographic vulnerability. Methods: Population-based retrospective cohort study (ICES, Ontario, Canada; 2007-2022). Adults surviving ICU admission for non-traumatic OHCA were matched to non-OHCA critical illness survivors by age (±3 years) and admission date (±3 days). Primary outcome: time to first new-onset MHA diagnosis within 15 years of discharge, from validated physician-coded inpatient, emergency department (ED), and outpatient records. We fit flexible parametric (Royston-Parmar) survival models with death as a competing risk and used logistic regression to compare inpatient versus outpatient care intensity, adjusting for sex, comorbidities, prior healthcare use, and neighbourhood marginalization. Results: Among 6,034 OHCA survivors matched to 16,461 controls (mean follow-up 4.7 years), 2,740 OHCA survivors (45.4%) received a new MHA diagnosis: anxiety/mood (33.9%), substance-related (7.8%), and psychotic disorders (2.7%); 20.0% required inpatient psychiatric admission. Incidence peaked within six months post-discharge. Composite MHA hazard was similar between cohorts (aHR 0.95; 95% CI 0.89-1.02). OHCA survivors had lower hazards for outpatient anxiety/mood (aHR 0.91), psychotic (0.74), and behavioural disorders (0.62); any inpatient psychiatric admission (0.85); inpatient mood disorders (0.69); and deliberate self-harm (0.73). The strongest predictor of new MHA outcomes was pre-existing psychiatric diagnosis (aHR 2.22; 95% CI 1.97-2.49); high pre-arrest ED use, younger age, female sex, and residence in racially marginalized or high-density neighbourhoods also independently predicted risk. Conclusions: Contrary to our hypothesis, OHCA survivors did not exhibit excess MHA risk versus matched critical illness survivors and showed lower hazards across several subcategories, suggesting shared post-ICU rather than arrest-specific psychiatric mechanisms. Nevertheless, nearly half developed a new MHA diagnosis, concentrated in the first six months and driven chiefly by pre-existing psychiatric history. These findings support integrating OHCA survivors into unified post-ICU mental health pathways, with early screening and targeted outreach for those with prior psychiatric diagnoses, high ED use, or residence in disadvantaged communities.
na3a0909f679c: Background: Survival following pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has improved, yet there is a paucity of research about the long-term outcomes and experiences of survivors and their families. Understanding their experiences will help shape survivor- and co-survivor-centered interventions and outcomes that focus on long-term recovery and well-being. Research Question: What is the lived experience of adolescent/young adult survivors (AYA) of OHCA and their parent co-survivors in survivorship? Aims: This study primarily sought to: (1) gain a deeper understanding of AYA survivors’ and their parents’/legal guardians’ perceptions of life after a CA in survivorship and (2) understand how survivors’ and co-survivors’ needs have changed over time since arrest. Methods: The study was conducted at a large pediatric healthcare system in Southern California using a qualitative phenomenological design. Participants were recruited using purposive, snowball, and convenience sampling. Eligible AYA were aged 10 to 24 years, English-speaking, experienced OHCA between ages 10-18, survived greater than 6 months post-arrest, and were able to verbally articulate their experiences. Parents/legal guardians of eligible AYA were also invited to participate. Each participant completed two semi-structured interviews between October 2025 and March 2026, which were audio-recorded and transcribed. Data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis informed by the hermeneutic circle. Coding was performed independently by two researchers, resolving discrepancies through consensus. Recruitment continued until thematic saturation was achieved. Results: Nine participants, including both survivors (n=3, 33.3%) and co-survivors (n=6, 66.6%), participated. Survivors were aged 18 to 24 years, and co-survivors were aged 40 to 59 years. Four (44.4%) self-identified as Hispanic or Latino. Five (55.5%) identified as White, two (22.2%) as Asian, and two (22.2%) as Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander. Among participants, four (44.4%) preferred “she” as their gender pronoun, three (33.3%) preferred “he,” and two (22.2%) preferred not to state. Five overarching themes about survivorship were identified: survivorship (a) is a new normal, (b) means being there, (c) is a physical embodiment, (d) means letting go, and (e) is what meaning we want to give it. Survivors emphasized challenges with self-concept and social reintegration, which is critical in their development stage. Parents described persistent anxiety, adjustment challenges, and advocacy burdens. Both groups highlighted discordance between acute care received and long-term support. Conclusions: AYA survivors of OHCA and their parents experience enduring psychosocial and functional impacts. Findings underscore the need for structured, family-centered, and individualized support throughout survivorship.
n4c664cca3d93: Background: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge, with persistent variation in outcomes across demographic and clinical subgroups. Evaluating recent trends in hospitalization and survival may identify disparities and inform targeted improvements in resuscitation systems of care. Methods: We conducted a retrospective trend analysis using the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) from 2019-2024. We evaluated temporal changes in (1) proportions of hospitalized OHCA patients across demographic and clinical characteristics and (2) survival to hospital discharge stratified by hospitalization-related factors.Generalized linear models with a Poisson distribution and log link were applied separately for each subgroup, with calendar year modeled as a continuous predictor and population at risk included as an offset. Deviance-based corrections accounted for overdispersion. Annual percentage changes with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated, with p<0.05 indicating statistical significance. Results: Significant shifts in OHCA hospitalization patterns were observed. The proportion of hospitalized female patients declined by 0.60% per year (95% CI, –0.76% to –0.45%; p<0.0001), while male hospitalizations increased by 0.37% per year (95% CI, 0.28% to 0.46%; p<0.0001). Hospitalizations among Black patients decreased modestly (–1.30% per year; 95% CI, –2.56% to –0.03%; p=0.045), whereas Hispanic/Latino patients demonstrated a substantial increase (4.94% per year; 95% CI, 2.17% to 7.79%; p=0.0004).Clinically, the proportion of patients achieving sustained return of spontaneous circulation declined (–2.58% per year; 95% CI, –4.41% to –0.72%; p=0.0066), while hospitalizations without sustained ROSC increased modestly. The proportion pronounced dead in the emergency department decreased significantly (–6.26% per year; 95% CI, –10.24% to –2.10%; p=0.0035).Despite these shifts, no subgroup demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in survival to discharge. Overall survival increased by 1.54% per year (95% CI, –2.18% to 5.39%; p=0.42), with similarly non-significant findings across arrest characteristics and hospitalization factors. Conclusions: From 2019 to 2024, OHCA hospitalization patterns shifted across demographic and clinical subgroups, with persistent disparities and declining sustained ROSC. Despite these changes, survival to hospital discharge has not significantly improved. These findings highlight ongoing inequities and underscore the need for targeted, system-level interventions to improve OHCA outcomes.
n0c968906ca0e: Introduction: Survivorship after cardiac arrest includes cognitive, emotional, and physical aspects of recovery. Domain specific recovery trajectories are individualized and under-reported in the literature. Understanding recovery capacity is critical for optimizing goal setting when counseling patients and their caregivers. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of comatose cardiac arrest survivors enrolled in our single-center acute brain injury repository between 2/5/2022 and 12/11/2025. We excluded patients who died prior to hospital discharge or who had no follow up modified Rankin Scale score (mRS). Patients were followed prospectively, and mRS was determined using patient and family interviews. Patients discharged alive with at least one follow-up mRS at any of the four time-points (3-month, 6-month, one year, two years) were included in the analysis. Good outcome was defined as mRS 0-3; longitudinal mRS changes were assessed with a Sankey plot. Results: Among the 56 patients [mean (SD) age 57.7 (16.8) years] included, 89.3% (n=50) were out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. The most common arrest etiology was cardiac (n = 36, 64.3%), of which the majority (n = 26, 72.2%) had a shockable rhythm, followed by respiratory (n = 15, 26.8%). Median (IQR) length of stay was 14 (9-22) days. The most common discharge locations were home (n=31, 55.4%) and short-term rehabilitation (n=14, 25%). Median (IQR) number of mRS assessments was 2 (2-3). Good outcome increased from 23 patients at three months to 26 patients at one year. There was one patient with poor outcome at one-year (mRS 4) who improved to good outcome at two years (mRS 0). In a sub-analysis of patients with an mRS at both 3-months and 1-year (n=11), 4 (36.4%) patients with mRS 2-3 improved to mRS 0-1. Conclusion: Functional neurologic recovery following cardiac arrest varies over time. Understanding recovery trajectories and factors associated with improvement are critical to maximizing survivorship potential. Our preliminary findings convey that recovery can be delayed, and possible up to two years following arrest.
ne85d4bae12e7: Introduction: Even among cardiac arrest survivors discharged with favorable neurologic outcomes, the risk of subsequent cardiac and non-cardiac complications, hospital re-admission, and mortality remains substantial. A better understanding of the causes and predictors of post-discharge re-admission and death is essential to developing targeted follow-up strategies, optimizing long-term recovery, and improving cardiac arrest survivorship. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of cardiac arrest survivors enrolled in a single center cardiac arrest recovery program (CARP) between 1/19/2024 and 5/9/2026. The CARP program follows all in-hospital (IHCA) and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients from index hospitalization admission to discharge, at which point those who awaken and were following basic commands were enrolled. Enrollment included an evaluation for psychological and cognitive symptoms, as well as post-discharge neurology clinic appointment (on average three months post-discharge). Amongst enrolled patients, hospital re-admissions and mortality occurring prior to post-discharge neurology clinic visit were tracked. Results: Of 105 enrolled patients, 34 (32.4%) underwent hospital readmission. The median [interquartile range] time from index cardiac arrest discharge to re-admission was 16 [8-99.8] days. Eight (7.6% of all patients, 24% of re-admitted patients) died at a median of 71.5 [20-160] days from index hospital discharge. The most common cause of death was withdrawal of life sustaining therapy (50%, n=4), followed by recurrent arrest without ROSC (25%, n=2). Amongst those who survived the readmission, the median [IQR] length of stay was 4 [2-10] days and the most common admission diagnoses included cardiopulmonary dysfunction (n=13, 38.2%) and neuropsychiatric symptoms (n=11, 32.4%). Patients requiring readmission were more likely to have suffered an IHCA, were younger, had longer length of stay, and were less likely to be discharged home (Table 1). Conclusion: Cardiac arrest survivors experience a heightened risk for readmission and mortality, even after discharge with good neurologic outcome. The most common causes for readmission were cardiopulmonary and neurologic symptoms. Further work to help identify those at highest risk for readmission and to evaluate the impact of a nurse navigator on readmission rate and mortality should be prioritized.
nf5864ea87956: Introduction: Functional outcomes after out-of-hospital-cardiac-arrest (OHCA) are often measured using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at a single time point, typically 90 days. While useful, this approach may miss meaningful changes in recovery that occur earlier in the post acute phase. Discharge location, whether home, a rehabilitation facility, a skilled nursing facility, or long term acute care, reflects a patient's recovery status, anticipated needs at the time of hospital discharge, and potentially with subsequent recovery trajectories. Methods: We performed a secondary analysis of ICECAP trial participants who completed mRS assessments at Day 90. We defined functional trajectories as improved when the Day 90 mRS was lower than at Day 30, stable when there was no change, or worsened when the Day 90 mRS was higher than Day 30. Outcomes were also grouped as favorable (mRS 0-3) or unfavorable (mRS 4-5), with changes examined by discharge location. Results: Among 1158 patients (median age 61 years, 40% female, 76% nonshockable rhythm), 276 had a documented discharge location with mRS assessed at Day 90. Discharge locations included home (53%), rehabilitation facility (18%), skilled nursing facility (12%), and long-term acute care (14%). Recovery trajectories varied substantially across discharge settings. Among patients discharged home, 57/146 (39%) improved, 52/146 (35.6%) remained stable, and 37/146 (25.3%) worsened between Day 30 and Day 90. Among patients discharged to rehabilitation facilities, 25/50 improved (50%), 19/50 remained stable (38%), and 6/50 worsened (12%). Those discharged to skilled nursing facilities had more mixed trajectories, 11/33 improved (33.3%), 18/33 remaining stable (54.5%), and 4/33 worsening (12.1%). In contrast, patients discharged to long term acute care were largely unchanged, with 31/38 stable (81.6%). Detailed recovery trajectories are shown in Figure 1. Conclusions: Functional recovery after OHCA continues to evolve between Day 30 and Day 90. Discharge location is associated with different recovery patterns and may offer early insight into a patient’s trajectory. These findings emphasize the importance of looking beyond a single 90 Day endpoint and suggest that discharge disposition can provide useful prognostic context.
nbca480931e65: Introduction: Post-anoxic status epilepticus (PASE) occurs in approximately one-third of comatose cardiac arrest (CA) survivors and is associated with high mortality. Although emerging evidence suggests favorable outcomes are achievable in a subset of patients, management is challenging and therapeutic nihilism may persist. In the absence of established management protocols, seizure monitoring and treatment practices may vary widely. Objective: To assess whether institutional protocol availability is associated with variation in management and electroencephalography (EEG)-based prognostication practices for PASE following CA. Methods: A cross-sectional Qualtrics survey was designed and approved for international dissemination (IRB #202300051) with assistance of professional societies between 2024-2026 to clinicians involved in PASE management. Responses were analyzed using question-specific denominators due to incomplete surveys. Exploratory protocol comparisons used Fisher exact tests. Results: Among 154 respondents, 27/95 (28%) reported having an institutional protocol, 61/95 (64%) reported no protocol, and 7/95 (7%) were unsure. Among those with protocols, 4/18 (22.2%) practiced in the United States, compared to 26/43 (60.5%) without protocols (p=0.011). ICU-based practice was less common among respondents with protocols versus without protocols (11/18 [61.1%] vs. 38/43 [88.4%], p=0.030). Continuous EEG use was higher among protocol respondents but non-significant (25/27 [92.6%] vs. 46/60 [76.7%], p=0.132). Monitoring all patients after return of spontaneous circulation was more common among respondents with protocols (10/27 [37.0%] vs. 10/60 [16.7%], p=0.053). The clearest differences were in EEG-based prognostic interpretation. Protocol respondents more often rated generalized periodic discharges within 24 hours as highly important for unfavorable prognosis (11/18 [61.1%] vs. 14/53 [26.4%], p=0.011). After 24 hours, they more often rated burst suppression as highly important (17/18 [94.4%] vs. 34/53 [64.2%], p=0.015). Escalation patterns were similar across groups, though intravenous non-anesthetic anti-seizure medications were selected less often, as first-choice therapy by respondents with protocols than those without protocols (7/23 [30.4%] vs. 29/58 [50.0%], p=0.140). Perceived benefits of early aggressive treatment were similar (3/18 [16.7%] vs. 8/53 [15.1%], p=1.000). Conclusion: PASE is largely managed without institutional protocols. Protocol availability was associated with differences in EEG-based prognostic interpretation, while treatment strategies and perceived benefits of aggressive treatment were similar. This suggests the key gap in PASE care may lie less in aggressive treatment and more in how clinicians interpret EEG patterns that guide prognostic judgment.
n0528f4de2f6b: Introduction: Cardiac arrest is the leading cause of cardiovascular mortality in the United States (US) with post-cardiac arrest anoxic brain injury (ABI) the leading cause of mortality among resuscitated survivors. Despite its high clinical and public health burden, national mortality trends and disparities in this subgroup of population remain largely uncharacterized. Aim: To evaluate national trends, demographic disparities and regional variations in mortality involving cardiac arrest and post cardiac arrest ABI among US adults from 1999 to 2024. Methods: We analyzed the CDC Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) for death certificates (1999-2024) of adults 25 years and older, with cardiac arrest (ICD: I46) and anoxic brain injury (ICD: G93). Age adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100,000 and annual percent change (APC) were calculated through join-point regression analysis. Results: Between 1999 and 2024 a total of 291,796 deaths involving cardiac arrest and ABI were reported. After an initial decline in AAMR from 4.35 in 1999 to 3.79 in 2004 (APC = –1.96%), a prolonged rise spanning two decades [APC = +3.77% (2004-2014), APC = +1.15% (2014-2021)] was observed, reaching a study peak of 6.10 in 2021. This represents a 40.2% increase from 2004 to 2021. Subsequently, AAMR declined to 4.96 in 2024 (13.8% above the 1999 baseline). Males consistently had a higher mortality than females. AAMR increased from 5.32 vs. 3.69 in 1999 to 6.21 vs. 3.90 in 2024. By 2024, female mortality had returned to near-baseline levels, whereas male mortality remained 16.7% above baseline. Non-Hispanic (NH) Black adults had the highest mortality burden with AAMR rising from 8.1 in 1999 to a peak of 12.9 in 2021. This group accounted for 59,322 total deaths, with a 2024 AAMR that remained 2.5-fold higher than that of NH Whites (10.85 vs. 4.31). NH American Indians demonstrated the largest relative increase in AAMRs (108% from 1999-2022). Region wise, the South consistently had the highest AAMR from 2013 onward, peaking at 6.99 in 2021 and was the region with highest AAMR in 2024 at 5.51. In 1999, urban areas had a higher AAMR than rural areas (4.51 vs. 3.72). However, by 2020, rural AAMR exceeded urban by 0.50-0.63 per 100,000. Although adults aged 65-74 years accounted for the largest number of deaths (74,200), crude mortality rate increased most rapidly among younger adults aged 25-34 years (+312%) and 35-44 years (+194%), while rates among adults ≥85 years declined by 47.8%. Conclusion: Between 1999 and 2024, mortality involving cardiac arrest and ABI demonstrated a sustained rise, with a peak in 2021. NH Blacks, NH American Indians, males, and residents of Southern states were disproportionately affected. The concurrent rise among younger adults warrants further investigation. These findings highlights the need for equitable post-resuscitation care and targeted policy interventions.
ne177a100128f: Background: Pseudo-subarachnoid hemorrhage (pseudo-SAH) and the white cerebellum sign are head CT findings that reflect severe hypoxic-ischemic brain injury following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). The clinical significance and outcomes have not been systemically characterized. Hypothesis: We hypothesize that these imaging findings signify poor neurological outcomes with important implications on goals-of-care discussions and neuroprognostication. Methods: This study is a retrospective case series of all adult OHCA patients presenting to four hospitals within the University of Pennsylvania Health System (2019-2024) under IRB approval #849677. Patients that had return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) with head CT findings of pseudo-SAH and white cerebellum sign were included for this study and corresponding arrest and outcome characteristics were collected from the electronic health record into a secured REDCap database. Primary outcome included in-hospital mortality and secondary outcomes encompassed cerebral performance category (CPC) and modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Results: Thirty-five patients were identified meeting the inclusion criteria: 30 (85.7%) with pseudo-SAH and 5 (14.3%) with white cerebellum sign. Mean age 53.6 ± 17.1 years; 45.7% female; 68.6% Black or African American. Non-shockable rhythms predominated (88.6%). CT co-findings included loss of gray-white differentiation and sulcal effacement (94.3% each), diffuse cerebral edema (91.4%), and herniation (20.0%). Neuron-specific enolase (NSE), available in 11 patients (31.4%) and was elevated (median 53.7 ng/mL [IQR 46.9-120.7]). Absent pupillary reflexes at 72 hours were documented in 78.3% and absent corneal reflexes at 72 hours in 87.5%. In-hospital mortality was 94.3% (33/35) in this group of patients. Both survivors had mRS 5 at discharge (CPC 3 and CPC 4, respectively); one died within three months post-OHCA. No patients achieved good neurological outcome (CPC 1-2 or mRS 0-2). Conclusions: This is the largest cohort in the literature describing pseudo-SAH and white cerebellum sign following OHCA. This study indicates that these findings are associated with very high in-hospital mortality and poor neurological recovery in the rare case of survival. These findings may serve as an early prognostic marker guiding neuroprognostication and goals-of-care discussions.
nbd6ac73d709e: Introduction: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy is the leading cause of mortality in adults who survive out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). While post-cardiac arrest ventilation and acid-base management are important to mitigate brain injury, the optimal resuscitation targets are unknown. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that perturbations in post-resuscitation blood carbon dioxide (PCO2) and pH would adversely impact 30-day mortality after OHCA. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of 2013-2024 data from Trinetx, a federated database of health records from >100 healthcare organizations and 100 million patients. We included adult patients with an emergency department of diagnoses of OHCA and who survived to hospital admission. Based on the mean PCO2 in the first 48 hours, we stratified patients by PCO2 (hypocapnia 30-50, normocapnia <30 and hypercapnia >50 mmHg) and pH (acidemic <7.3, normal physiologic 7.3-7.5, alkalotic >7.5). The primary outcome was 30-day death. Using Cox proportional hazards regression, we evaluated the associations of PCO2 and pH with 30-day death, adjusting for age, sex and past medical history. Results: Of 88,754 OHCA patients admitted to hospitals, we included 36,176 adults with complete data. Median age was 64 (IQR 52-74), and 13,176 (37.9%) were female. Initial PCO2s were 30-50 (66.6%), <30 (10.3%), and >50 (23.1%). Initial pHs were 7.3-7.5 (51.8%), <7.3 (46.4%), and >7.5 (1.8%). Compared with normocapnia, risk of 30-day death was higher for sustained hypocapnia PCO2<30 (aHR=1.2, 95% CI 1.2-1.3) and for hypercapnia PCO2>50 (aHR=1.2, 95% CI 1.2-1.3). Compared with normal physiologic acid-base status, risk of death was higher for acidosis pH<7.3 (aHR=1.6, 95% CI 1.6-1.7) but not for sustained alkalosis pH>7.5 (aHR=1.0, 95% CI 0.9-1.2). Conclusion: In the early post-arrest period, sustained exposure to hypercapnia, hypocapnia, and acidosis were associated with worse 30-day mortality. Post-arrest management of ventilation and acid-base status are important in the care of OHCA.
n4e7241aa5a41: Introduction: Low-income patients experience worse outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Little is known about disparities in post-arrest hospital care that may contribute to these outcome disparities. We sought to identify income-based disparities in post-arrest care. Hypothesis: Lower income patients have worse hospital outcomes and receive post-arrest care less often. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed the 2019-2022 National Emergency Department Sample, a national claims database. We included adult patients who survived to admission and excluded those with missing data. We stratified patients based on their household income quartile. We defined outcomes as post-arrest care, survival to discharge, and discharge to home (a surrogate for a good neurologic outcome). Using ordinal logistic regression, we evaluated the association between decreasing income quartile and outcomes with the top income quartile defined as the reference. We adjusted the analyses for age, sex, and race. Results: Of 359,652 OHCAs, 198,785 survived to admission. We included 188,627 patients; 32,534 from the top, 40,661 from the 2 nd , 49,751 from the 3 rd , and 65,681 from the lowest income quartile. Discharge to home rates for each group were 19.6% for 1 st , 19.1% for 2 nd , 17.9% for 3 rd , and 16.4% for 4 th income quartiles. Decreasing income was associated with decreased odds of left heart catheterization (OR 0.81 [0.77-0.85]), percutaneous coronary intervention (OR 0.85 [0.81-0.89]), ventricular assist device (OR 0.77 [0.71-0.83]), automatic implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (OR 0.85 [0.81-0.89]), extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (OR 0.55 [0.45-0.68]), coronary artery bypass graft (OR 0.84 [0.75-0.94]), echocardiography (OR 0.85 [0.76-0.95]), central line placement (OR 0.93 [0.89-0.97]), arterial line placement (OR 0.86 [0.79-0.97]), therapeutic hypothermia (OR 0.70 [0.56-0.86]), survival (OR 0.90 [0.87-0.93]) , and survival with discharge to home (OR 0.87 [0.83-0.90]). Decreasing income was not associated with decreased odds of Head CT, electroencephalogram, body CT, or do not resuscitate orders. Conclusion: Decreasing income was associated with decreased odds of cardiac procedures, resuscitative procedures, and OHCA outcomes. Our findings suggest that income-based disparities in post-arrest care exist and warrant further investigation.
n8cb616eabf5e: Background: Analgesia and sedation are key components of post-cardiac-arrest care and facilitate temperature control; however, limited data describe their safety. We evaluated the association between time to awakening (T2A) and cumulative dose of analgosedation (AS). Methods: We performed a retrospective, cohort study of adults with non-traumatic in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) or out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) between January 2021 and November 2025 at three Seattle, WA hospitals. Patients who awoke prior to 24 hours were excluded. The primary exposure was cumulative AS dose given during comatose hours in the first 96 hours of hospitalization. Cumulative doses were normalized to patient weight and number of comatose minutes. The primary outcome was T2A, with awake defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale-Motor score of 6. The secondary outcome was achieving wakefulness. Outcomes were adjusted for covariates (age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, OHCA vs IHCA, seizures within the first 96 hours, shock on admission) and were analyzed using Cox regression and logistic regression, respectively. A time-varying coefficient was used for propofol due to a proportional hazards violation. Results: Of 855 eligible adults, 26 (3%) received barbiturates or dexmedetomidine and were excluded. Of the remaining 829, 141 (17%) awoke. Higher cumulative benzodiazepine exposure was associated with slower T2A (HR=0.37, 95% CI 0.17-0.83, p=0.015) and decreased chance of awakening (OR=0.19, 95% CI 0.07-0.51, p=0.001). Higher cumulative propofol exposure was associated with faster T2A, and this association was time-dependent, showing strongest effect at 6 hours (HR=6.45, 95% CI 2.46-10.44, p=0.0015) and attenuating by day 7 (HR=2.01, 95% CI 1.47-2.55, p<0.0001); it was also associated with an increased chance of awakening (OR=4.33, 95% CI 3.21-5.84, p<0.001). Opioid exposure was not significantly associated with T2A (HR=1.05, 95% CI 0.95-1.16, p=0.343) or chance of awakening (OR=1.24, 95% CI 0.99-1.56, p=0.061). Conclusions: In non-traumatic OHCA and IHCA, higher cumulative benzodiazepine exposure was associated with longer T2A and lower overall chance of awakening, whereas higher cumulative propofol exposure was associated with faster T2A and higher chance of awakening. Opioid exposure was not significantly associated with awakening metrics. Given the observational nature of this study, these findings cannot definitively establish causality, and confounding may remain where patients with greater illness severity required higher AS doses.
n33d7f579c0c8: Background: Post-arrest hypotension, typically defined by the lowest systolic blood pressure (SBP), is associated with mortality after pediatric cardiac arrest. However, many post-arrest patients require vasopressors and inotropes, and prior analyses have not accounted for SBP together with vasoactive support intensity. Research Question: Among children after cardiac arrest, is Vasoactive Inotropic Score (VIS) and a derived ratio of VIS to SBP associated with mortality, and does incorporation of VIS improve outcome discrimination beyond SBP alone? Aim: We aimed to 1) create a composite term to account for both SBP and VIS called Hemodynamic Index (HI; a calculated ratio of simultaneously measured SBP to VIS) and 2) explore the relationship between SBP, VIS and HI and mortality after pediatric cardiac arrest. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed children < 18 years who initially survived IHCA and OHCA lasting > 1 minute cared for in our single-center pediatric intensive care unit with pathway-guided SBP targets. We collected lowest percentile-corrected SBP and peak VIS in multiple time intervals (0-24, 0-48- and 0-72 hour epochs post-arrest). We created 3 equations to calculate HI in this exploratory analysis (Figure 1). Outcome was hospital mortality. For this preliminary analysis, we performed univariate analysis to determine association of each predictor with mortality. To assess prediction of SBP, VIS and HI for mortality, we calculated unadjusted areas under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Results: Of 793 patients, IHCA occurred in 63%, and mortality in 38%. Median age was 1.8 (IQR 0.4-8.0) years, and arrest duration was 7.4 (IQR 2-21) minutes. On univariate analysis, VIS and HI were associated with increased odds of mortality (p<0.001, Table 1). VIS demonstrated the strongest precision-recall performance for mortality (AUPRC 0.622 at 0-24 h, 0.634 at 0-48 h, and 0.642 at 0-72 h), followed by HI 1 and HI 2, while HI 3 showed weaker discrimination. SBP showed only modest improvement over the mortality prevalence baseline, indicating limited discriminative utility. Conclusions: In this exploratory single-center analysis of children after cardiac arrest, peak VIS was more strongly associated with mortality than SBP alone or the derived HI models. Further work is needed to refine composite hemodynamic measures and to determine if accounting for the interaction between blood pressure and vasoactive support improves hemodynamic assessment after pediatric cardiac arrest.
nc18f6dcf01b1: Introduction: While ACLS has optimized CPR, post-ROSC care lacks targeted interventions for endophenotypes. Precision resuscitation requires moving beyond static baseline risk. By leveraging EMR data to quantify dynamic trajectories of immuno-metabolic biomarkers from pre-arrest to post-ROSC, we characterized active physiological shifts to identify treatable in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) endophenotypes. Methods: This IRB-exempt study (January 2020-January 2026) evaluated adult patients undergoing CPR for IHCA within 48h of admission who achieved ROSC and survived in the ICU for >24h. Sequential clustering integrated Elixhauser Comorbidity Categories with pre-arrest biomarkers. Within derived clusters, Boosted Tree models quantified the variance explained (VE%) for a composite outcome (CO) (Hospice DC or Hospital Mortality) using delta ( D) (pre-IHCA to post-ROSC/ICU Day 1) of 22 biomarker predictors. Results: Among 435 patients, five distinct clinical endophenotypes were identified with divergent clinical profiles, host support requirements, and survival rates (Table 1). Boosted tree modeling demonstrated cluster-specific risk was driven by biological mechanisms (Figure 1): Cluster 1 (Immune Mobilization; n=239, 55%): A predominant, intermediate-risk phenotype with variance heavily driven by the acute mobilization of immature myeloid lineages ( D Promyelocytes, Myelocytes, and Metamyelocytes). Cluster 2 (Cardiorenal Frailty; n=103, 24%): An elderly cohort characterized by valvular and renal multimorbidity, where outcomes were primarily dictated by acute protein-vascular shifts ( D Albumin and D Platelet Count). Cluster 3 (Vascular/Capillary Leak; n=19, 4%): A high-mortality, low-support phenotype uniquely driven by microvascular barrier degradation and capillary leak ( D Albumin/Creatinine Ratio). Cluster 4 (Metabolic Exhaustion; n=58, 13%): A younger, lower-mortality cohort where outcome variance was almost exclusively explained by bioenergetic failure and altered anaerobic pathways ( D Lactate/Glucose and D Glucose/Albumin Ratios). Cluster 5 (Endothelial Collapse; n=16, 4%): A hyper-acute, high-risk phenotype presenting with dense baseline CHF and hepatic disease, exhibiting severe, symmetrical immuno-metabolic disruptions and profound endothelial degradation ( D Albumin x Platelet Product and D Neutrophil/Albumin Ratio). Conclusions: Coupling structural multimorbidity with functional biomarker trajectories operationalizes treatable traits. This approach allows standard ACLS pathways to be enhanced by targeted, phase-specific interventions. Transitioning targeted therapies into the immediate post-ROSC window could rescue specific bioenergetic (Cluster 4) or endothelial collapse (Cluster 5) phenotypes before secondary reperfusion injury becomes irreversible.
nd8b0fb95daaf: Background: For refractory ventricular fibrillation (rVF), two strategies have been studied in separate clinical trials: intra-arrest transport (IAT) to Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (ECPR) and Double Sequential External Defibrillation (DSED). However, some systems have both treatments available, and the optimal time to stop DSED and start IAT to ECPR remains unclear. Aim: We aimed to describe the probability of prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) with ongoing DSED in patients still pulseless at three time points in the resuscitation and the proportion of pulseless patients already undergoing IAT at these times. Methods: We included patients randomized to DSED in secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial who did not have prehospital termination of resuscitation, vector change shocks prior to DSED, or a missing time of fourth defibrillation. We calculated the probability of prehospital ROSC at or beyond minute 5, 10, and 15 post-fourth defibrillation (first randomized DSED shock) in those still pulseless and the proportion already undergoing IAT. Results: Of 125 patients, 118 were included after applying exclusion criteria. Of these 118 patients, 58 (49%) achieved prehospital ROSC with 53/58 (91%) occurring on scene. At minutes 5, 10, and 15 post-fourth-defibrillation the probability of ROSC with continued resuscitation was 32/96 (33%), 16/80 (20%), and 7/71 (10%) respectively. At these same time points, the proportion of pulseless patients undergoing IAT was 2/96 (2%), 10/80 (13%), and 23/70 (33%) were actively undergoing IAT. Conclusions: The optimal timing of IAT in a system providing both ECPR and DSED may be from minutes 10-15, as the proportion of patients who will get ROSC falls below 10% at 15 minutes post-fourth-defibrillation; however, 32% of patients were receiving IAT at this timepoint, potentially underestimating the yield of continued on-scene resuscitation.
nf98ca3526171: Introduction: Intra-arrest transport (IAT) of out of hospital cardiac arrest is associated with worse patient outcomes compared to on-scene resuscitation. However, on-scene resuscitation is difficult to sustain as family distress may impact clinical decision-making, requiring a structured approach to supporting families and family presence during resuscitation. Research Questions: To what extent does family presence influence EMS clinician decision-making regarding IAT? What impact does family-focused training have on EMS clinician confidence in managing resuscitation in the presence of family members? Aims: Describe EMS clinician perceptions of how the presence of family may influence IAT decision-making. Develop and pilot a family life support (FLS) training program and evaluate its impact on EMS clinician confidence in performing pre-defined competencies. Methods: We created a FLS training program with didactic and simulation education within a single, rural EMS agency. A pre-post survey with Likert scale evaluated clinician confidence in four identified competencies. A Wilcoxon signed rank test was performed to determine significance. Rapid thematic analysis was performed on open text responses. Results: A total of 73 EMS clinicians participated; 64% reported that the presence of family members did not influence IAT decision making, 36% were somewhat influenced in their decision and 7% reported a direct influence. Five themes described how family presence influences IAT decision-making: decisions driven by protocol alone, contextual considerations, ability to communicate with the family, scene safety, and ethical beliefs regarding family perspectives. After FLS training, there was a significant improvement in EMS clinicians’ confidence in guiding a family member through a resuscitation event (4.10 ± 0.97 v 4.48 ± 0.69,p <0.001). There were no statistically significant changes in confidence in communication, leading a pause, or empathizing with family. Participants described wanting to be more inclusive of family in future resuscitations (24%,9/37), improve communication with family (49%,18/37), and implement a pause in the case of patient death (14%,5/37). Narrative responses described high perceived value in the training and a strong preference for experiential learning. Conclusion: Family presence influences some EMS clinicians’ IAT decision-making. The FLS training program improved EMS clinicians' confidence in skills to guide families through a resuscitation.
n3d33e31c5abd: Background: Prehospital airway management, including prehospital endotracheal intubation (PETI), is an important component of prehospital trauma care for patients with severe trauma. Previous studies evaluating the association between PETI and mortality have reported conflicting results, potentially due to variability in provider expertise, patient selection, and healthcare systems. Japan has a physician-staffed emergency medical service system, including helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) and ground emergency medical services (GEMS), in which emergency physicians provide prehospital advanced airway management. Therefore, the aim of this study was to evaluate the association between physician-performed PETI and in-hospital mortality. Hypothesis: Physician-performed PETI would be associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with IETI. Methods: This multicenter retrospective cohort study analyzed data from the Japan Trauma Data Bank, a nationwide trauma registry, between 2019 and 2023. Adult trauma patients (18 years or older) directly transported from the injury scene to participating hospitals by physician-staffed HEMS or GEMS were eligible. Patients with a clinical indication for endotracheal intubation defined by respiratory failure, shock, or impaired consciousness, who underwent PETI or IETI were included. Patients with cardiac arrest at the scene and those with burns were excluded.The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included scene time and total transportation time. Inverse probability weighting (IPW) with propensity scores was used to adjust for patient demographics, prehospital vital signs, and injury severity. The association between PETI and in-hospital mortality was evaluated using IPW-adjusted logistic regression. Several subgroup analyses by intubation indication were performed to evaluate the consistency of the findings across patients with respiratory failure, shock, or impaired consciousness. Results: Among 1,253 patients (median age, 68 years; 76% male; median Injury Severity Score, 26), 370 (30%) underwent PETI and 883 (70%) underwent IETI. PETI was not associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with IETI (37% vs 34%; adjusted odds ratio, 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.91-1.51; p=0.226). PETI was associated with a longer scene time (median difference, 9 minutes; 95% CI, 7-11; p<0.001) and longer total transportation time (median difference, 13 minutes; 95% CI, 10-17; p<0.001). Subgroup analyses across intubation indication showed consistent results. Conclusions: In this nationwide cohort of trauma patients transported by physician-staffed emergency medical services, PETI was not associated with lower in-hospital mortality compared with IETI and was associated with longer scene and total transportation times.
nde4892735d4f: Introduction: Pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a high-acuity, low-occurrence event with persistently poor survival and neurologic outcomes. Optimal airway management during pediatric OHCA remains uncertain, as high-quality evidence comparing endotracheal intubation (ETI) with less invasive alternatives such as bag-valve-mask (BVM) ventilation or supraglottic airway (SGA) devices is limited. Hypothesis: Prehospital ETI is associated with improved outcomes compared to non-ETI airway management. Aims: To evaluate the association between prehospital ETI and clinical outcomes in children with OHCA. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of subjects aged 30 days to 18 years with OHCA transported by emergency medical services (EMS) to the only quaternary pediatric emergency department serving a large metropolitan area with over 50 EMS agencies . Patients with tracheostomy or cricothyroidotomy were excluded. Subjects were stratified by final airway management strategy prior to ED arrival: prehospital ETI versus non-ETI airway management (BVM and/or SGA without ETI). Patient demographics, arrest characteristics, and prehospital interventions were compared using Kruskal-Wallis and chi-square analyses. Primary outcomes were return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and survival to hospital discharge (SHD). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between ETI and outcomes, adjusting for age, initial rhythm, and witnessed arrest status. Results: Among 203 included patients, 40 (20%) underwent prehospital ETI. The cohort was predominantly infants (median age 0.7 years, IQR 0.2 - 4.3), with mostly unwitnessed arrests (75%) and non-shockable rhythms (94%). Patients receiving ETI were older (median age 2.5 vs 0.4 years, p<0.001) and received more epinephrine doses (median 4 vs 2, p<0.001). Unadjusted outcomes were numerically higher in the ETI group, including ROSC (32.5% vs. 26.4%) and SHD (12.5% vs. 8.0%). However, after adjustment, ETI was not independently associated with ROSC (aOR 1.32, 95% CI 0.57-2.91) or SHD (aOR 1.56, 95% CI 0.44-4.85). Shockable initial rhythm was independently associated with both ROSC (aOR 5.98, 95% CI 1.54-29.5) and SHD (aOR 5.54, 95% CI 1.26-23.3), while witnessed arrest was associated with ROSC (aOR 2.42, 95% CI 1.14-5.07). Conclusion: In this single-center cohort of pediatric OHCA, prehospital ETI was not independently associated with improved ROSC or survival to hospital discharge. Patients undergoing ETI demonstrated characteristics suggestive of greater arrest severity, raising the possibility of residual confounding by indication. These findings underscore the need for multicenter studies and improved physiologic characterization of pediatric OHCA to better define optimal airway management strategies.

nd0396a258a54: Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. Cohort study using the target trial framework. Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. Possible residual confounding. Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. Research Council of Norway.

n03e5666e9269: Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time. To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC. Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]). 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico. 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection. The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points. An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar. Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement. Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials. National Institutes of Health.

n36711ffe3a9c: One critical shortcoming of many clinical therapeutic trials is their focus on short-term effects, leaving unanswered questions about how participants fare in the longer term. Trial extension studies are conducted to address this gap, allowing assessment of both durability of treatment benefit (eg, whether disease remission or improvements in function are maintained or diminished over time) and long-term safety (such as incidence of delayed adverse events). In therapeutic trials, extension studies can mitigate the ethical burden associated with discontinuation of potentially effective treatments or long-term administration of placebo or inferior interventions among those initially assigned to the control group. The prospect of an extension study may also give participants greater incentive to enroll in trials, despite concerns about being assigned to the control group in the initial phase of the research. Because extension studies build on existing trial infrastructure, they also allow additional and potentially valuable information to be derived from trials that already require significant up-front investment.

n301b4b9cd03d: If medicine too readily imagines the body as machine, the poem “Eternal life” proposes poetry itself as a deeper, more marvelously humane technology. Against a searchable database and a website’s archived obituary photographs, the poem offers its own elegant processing, synthesis, and preservation, which do not merely confirm whether someone has died, but restore the departed in the small gestures that make each one memorably human. Thus an implicit comparison emerges, with medicine’s view of decline and mortality as mechanical failure and retrievable data points contrasted with poetry’s returning of meaning, not a device for defeating or quantifying death, but a form for giving the deceased back to consciousness. The phone downloads a photograph and the website records a name as seamlessly as physicians might imagine how the brain stores and recalls memories. Yet neither can revivify the people the speaker’s father once knew, as it takes poetry to deliver the sweet sharing of sugar and the click of a returned key unlocking a door. The familiar medical fantasy of cybernetic immortality through synchronicity conquering biological decay is replaced by the strange kindness of poetry’s perfectly imperfect recollection, with loved ones absent at one moment but then lucidly present again the next. Forgetting, medically construed as neurological malfunction, becomes instead a porous border across which the dead may return through poetry’s dream-making. Poetry ultimately offers its own godlike machinery: “A last untouched memory/That kept giving them back to you/Eternally” concludes the poem, as if granting the eternal life announced in its title.

n9e1955af9b2e: Prescription drug manufacturers typically apply to the US Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) for patents to protect their products from generic competition. The primary patent on a drug covers the core active ingredient and generally lasts 20 years. Because these patents are often granted early in drug development, however, the effective period of patent protection after US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval is usually 7 to 12 years. Once that period ends, generic versions may enter the market and compete with the brand-name drug, often leading to a rapid and substantial decline in price. The statutory framework for drug patents is established in the Hatch-Waxman Act of 1984. In addition to patent protection, brand-name drugs may qualify for periods of exclusivity granted by the FDA, which may run concurrently with patents or separately.

ne9e8bae073bb: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs. In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446). Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers. These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings. nf91dcde14822: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. n6e0fa2420828: The rapid worldwide spread of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria is driven by a complex interplay of human, environmental, and health care-associated factors and accelerated by mobile genetic elements that facilitate the dissemination of resistance genes. Clinically important resistant pathogens include extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. n614e43669602: To the Editor The Viewpoint article by Drs Singh and Mello provides a balanced discussion of advertising in artificial intelligence (AI)–powered clinical decision support (CDS). It is worth highlighting that the authors state that AI-powered CDS often is free. Did we not say the same about drug company–sponsored lunches and so-called “free” pens and other giveaways in the 1990s? Some will recall when drug companies sponsored lunches for faculty and trainees, gave away pens and other branded items, and sometimes accompanied physicians on rounds. For those who trained more recently, please know that this practice was widely accepted; however, we eventually learned that there is, in fact, no free lunch. Now, we must learn there is no free CDS. Singh and Mello note that while “some products operate on a subscription model, others such as OpenEvidence use advertising revenue to offer access without charge.” It is surprising and disappointing that clinicians may think they are receiving CDS for free. Perhaps they have forgotten—or may have never learned—that drug company advertisements influence prescribing behavior when they appear alongside information intended to educate physicians and support clinical practice. Clearly the drug companies themselves have not forgotten. Twenty years ago, the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations revised its code of ethics and barred gifts or money that could influence prescribing behavior. CDS companies that embed pharmaceutical advertisements in their products should end this practice and, if they do not, the pharmaceutical industry should do so. Better yet, clinicians should recognize they have other options without industry advertisements and should choose such CDS tools.
ndd27c90df34d: In Reply We appreciate the thoughtful letters in response to our Viewpoint. n1bce3d09872e: “Do I need to treat this blood pressure?” is one of the most common questions to pass through the minds of acute care pediatricians during a typical day in the hospital. As a result of interindividual variation across the developmental stages of childhood, there is a wide range of acceptable blood pressure values. There is also long-standing ambiguity about what should be considered the limits of acceptable blood pressure, particularly among hospitalized children. Financing showed the largest gaps-only five of eleven financing sub-elements had median scores of 1·0 or less.InterpretationOur analysis suggests that NCCP comprehensiveness varies substantially between countries with consistent weaknesses in financing, outcome measurement, and contextual analysis. A shared health systems framework and scalable AI appraisal tools, such as PRISM, could support more complete, comparable, and actionable plans to strengthen cancer control globally by providing the possibility for rapid analysis of comprehensiveness of NCCPs and generation of timely, achievable, and evidence-informed, context-specific plans that use the latest data.FundingHarvard University.
neb745a437649: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.
n9b8e8ddc7353: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. Using an evidence-based approach, a standardised guideline for referral for cancer genetics evaluation of childhood cancer survivors at high risk of having a CPS was developed and incorporated into the Children's Oncology Group Long-Term Follow-Up Guidelines for Survivors of Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancers. This Policy Review details the importance, development, and anticipated impact of this new guideline. Raising awareness of this guideline is crucial to enhancing the integration of genetics into survivorship care and improving health outcomes for childhood cancer survivors with CPS.
n499627ac072d: BackgroundAnti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; pInterpretationThe risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.FundingMiltenyi Biomedicine.
ne805cbc8e893: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; PConclusionsAmong patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. nc84ddc78d69c: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). nf41e676512a9: BackgroundPembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.MethodsIn this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. n365a6c6e67cf: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). n13e34fe4211f: BackgroundThe combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. n44e6f9b772f2: BackgroundThe standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. nc53d4fc9dded: A 14-day schedule of FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD–TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.
naabad6018a64: Offering late-line systemic therapy to patients with chemo-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer demands a careful estimation of the balance between the expected treatment benefit and its potential impact on quality of life, including adverse events, hospital visits, and psychosocial consequences.1 In such a comprehensive and individualised assessment of patients’ general conditions, usually summarised by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, the cumulative burden of disease-related symptoms and previous treatment-related adverse events, together with the potential decay of organ functional reserve, cannot be neglected.
n37e38146b6c7: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.
neade2a36331e: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.
n4151c8f48c2e: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24).…
n51921c6a91ab: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.
n44febee54942: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.
n2f70a03ce0f8: Heavy menstrual bleeding is a challenging condition that, when refractory to conventional treatment, frequently culminates in hysterectomy. Endometrial ablation offers an effective, uterus-sparing alternative for women who do not desire future childbearing, with lower perioperative morbidity and faster recovery than hysterectomy.1–3 However, the durability of this procedure can be variable. Residual endometrium can result in recurrent bleeding or cyclical pelvic pain requiring further treatment, with approximately one in ten women undergoing hysterectomy within 2 years.
n7782c90086eb: For decades, the standard of care for patients with resected stage II and III colon cancer has centred on surgery with consideration of postoperative adjuvant systemic therapy to reduce risk of recurrence. Mismatch repair deficiency is seen in 10–15% of non-metastatic colon cancers and is predictive of response to immune checkpoint inhibition. The initial report of the single-arm, phase 2 NICHE-2 study of one dose of ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) and two doses of nivolumab (3 mg per kg) before surgery with clinical stage II and III colon cancer generated considerable interest after demonstrating a remarkable 98% pathologic response rate, including a pathologic complete response rate of 68%.
nf56aff0ef588: BackgroundMedicare Advantage insurers conduct in-home health risk assessments (HRAs) to identify high-risk patients and facilitate appropriate care. Observed differences in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions across encounter settings may be susceptible to unmeasured confounding.ConclusionAmong Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, an increasingly large share of cardiovascular conditions are being diagnosed through in-home HRAs, but treatment rates after these diagnoses are consistently lower than after facility-based encounters.Primary funding sourceNational Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.
n98f014590d8e: BackgroundThe Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use.ConclusionThe LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. na94264d40dc8: BackgroundThe United States recently proposed changes to the recommendations for childhood hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccination.ObjectiveTo project the effect of vaccine policy changes, if fully implemented, on chronic HBV infections.DesignMarkov cohort state transition model of perinatal and childhood HBV infection.Data sourcesPublished data on maternal HBV prevalence (0.4%) and hepatitis B surface antigen testing (99.5% sensitivity), childhood vaccine completion (universal birth-dose strategy: 91.1%; deferred strategy: 87.1%; shared decision-making strategy: 50.0%), and age-stratified risk for chronic HBV infection.Target populationOne-year birth cohort of U.S.-born infants (n = 3.6 million).Time horizon20 years.InterventionUniversal birth-dose vaccination, deferred (2-month) vaccination, and vaccination through shared decision making.Outcome measuresNumbers with chronic HBV infection and susceptibility to HBV, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) derived from probabilistic sensitivity analysis.Results of base-case analysisCompared with the universal birth-dose strategy (255 childhood infections [95% UI, 130 to 530]), the deferred and shared decision-making strategies would increase chronic HBV infections in the 2026 birth cohort by 19% to 303 (95% UI, 155 to 610) and by 83% to 467 (95% UI, 209 to 1032), respectively. n1b491eba192b: The Hindu Kush Himalayan region, also known as the Third Pole, is warming faster than the global average, with mountain environments experiencing particularly rapid climatic change and climatic extremes.1 The potential risks of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) have been documented for decades, with 47 glacial lakes at risk of expansion and causing GLOFs located in the Hindu Kush Himalayan region, including 21 in Nepal.2 The Rasuwa-Bhote Koshi flood of Aug 26, 2026, near the China–Nepal border, resulted in a catastrophic flood travelling at a speed of 188 km/h from its source; the flood covered 20 km within 7–8 min and reached the China–Nepal border at Rasuwagadhi.

nc323dcc0f863: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. By contrast, antibody-mediated disorders targeting neuronal antigens (ie, autoimmune encephalitides) are still frequently analysed collectively, with data from different disorders pooled as if they represent a single disease rather than distinct entities. Such interdisciplinary collaboration facilitates the recognition of new diseases and elucidation of the causes of previously unclassified disorders. n5729197f38e9: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. n1d8ac6a16ca9: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.

n22a7e8b53682: In many disease settings, physicians and patients can choose between several treatment options that are in common use, but how should they make the choice? nb8510b0ee181: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis—a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. n9ace97f52042: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century.
